title: Wave numbers are a run-start snapshot, but the window enforces them as if live
description:
THE reason runs go sequential. Observed live in epic ncv, 2026-09-18.

The run reads the epic graph ONCE (reconcile.go: graph := r.tracker.Graph(...); plan := planFrom(graph)) and hands that plan to runPlan. tk assigns wave numbers by layering the dependency graph AT THAT MOMENT, so a tick whose blocker is still open is recorded in a LATER wave.

mayAdmit then refuses to mix waves:

    if isRoleJob(fl.entry.Role) || fl.entry.Wave != next.Wave { return false }

That rule is right for real waves and wrong for stale ones. When a blocker closes mid-run, its dependents do not move up — they stay stranded in a wave number that describes a graph that no longer exists.

Measured here. The run resumed at 16:31:54 with z23 still open, so the snapshot put vyg in wave 2 alone and 9fc/ef7 in a later wave. z23 closed at 16:39:57. Fifteen minutes later, with THREE free slots and both ticks ready, 9fc and ef7 had still not been dispatched — they appear ZERO times in the run's 100-event feed. A fresh read of the same graph says:

    Wave 1 (ready now) (3 parallel)
      9fc, ef7, vyg          <- all three, same wave
    Dispatch: 1 in flight, 3 slot(s) free

So the work is ready, the slots are free, and the plan is the only thing saying no.

The cost is one full run incarnation per dependency edge. Every time a blocker closes, the run drains, finishes, and a person restarts it to re-plan. That is the 'we have gone very sequential' complaint, and tick 5fx's dispatch window cannot fix it: 5fx made ticks ALREADY in one wave run together, while this strands the ticks that just became peers.

Work:
- Re-read the graph when an in-flight attempt settles, and re-derive waves. The plan is a view, not a ledger; the tracker is the authority, and the run already re-reads it per tick in settleBeforeDispatch.
- Keep the wave boundary as a SEMANTIC rule (do not start work that depends on unfinished work) rather than a numeric one. A tick whose blockers are all closed is admissible regardless of the number it carried at run start.
- Do not lose the composition checks: re-planning must re-run checkWaveComposition, not skip it.
- Test: one wave's tick closes while another is in flight; its dependents must be admitted WITHOUT a restart.

Related: 5fx (the window itself), h74 (same-wave file safety).
acceptance_criteria: A tick whose blockers close while the run is live is dispatched by that same run, with no restart, and a test covers exactly that sequence
